Hot Mulled Cider for Wassail

Served at: Old Twelfth Night Wassail

Serves 8-10Prep 10 minCook 25 min

This warming Hot Mulled Cider is a quintessential beverage for Old Twelfth Night Wassail, a traditional English custom to bless apple orchards and ensure a good harvest. Served steaming hot, it's perfect for toasting good health and prosperity during the mid-winter festivities, bringing cheer and comfort to all gathered.

Ingredients

  • 1 gallon (3.8 L) apple cider, unfiltered preferred
  • 1 large orange, thinly sliced
  • 4 cinnamon sticks
  • 1 tablespoon whole cloves
  • 1 teaspoon whole allspice berries
  • 2 star anise pods
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) maple syrup or brown sugar (optional, to taste)
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) brandy or dark rum (optional, for adult versions)

Method

  1. Pour the apple cider into a large, non-reactive pot or Dutch oven.
  2. Add the orange slices, cinnamon sticks, whole cloves, allspice berries, and star anise pods to the cider.
  3. If using, stir in the maple syrup or brown sugar until dissolved.
  4. Heat the mixture over medium heat until it just begins to simmer. Do not boil, as this can diminish the flavor of the spices.
  5. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and let the cider gently simmer for at least 20 minutes to allow the flavors to meld and deepen.
  6. Before serving, if desired, stir in the brandy or dark rum.
  7. Strain the cider through a fine-mesh sieve to remove the spices and orange slices, or leave them in for presentation.
  8. Serve hot in mugs, garnished with a fresh orange slice or cinnamon stick if desired.

Tips

  • For a stronger spice flavor, gently crush the whole spices slightly before adding them to the cider.
  • This mulled cider can be kept warm in a slow cooker on the 'warm' setting for several hours, perfect for extended celebrations.
  • Adjust the sweetness to your liking; taste before adding any sweetener, as cider sweetness varies.
